newsitem.title: UK: Shell seen edging to closure of French refinery. [CORRECTED 15:47 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Shell seen edging to closure of French refinery. [CORRECTED 15:47 GMT]

text.p: As French oil workers went on strike in Shell's Berre l'Etang oil refinery in southern France to protest against industry rationalisation, oil analysts said Shell moved a step towards closing the plant.

Shell said in a statement on Tuesday that it would issue a memorandum of understanding to the French authorities by end January 1997 on its proposals for its operations in south-east France (corrects reference to refinery from "its proposals for Berre l'Etang"). Analysts said the carefully worded announcement was another step towards closing the 120,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) plant.
Shell said it was actively evaluating its options after a French industry study recommended capacity rationalisation in France.
"In Shell's view, the first objective of rationalisation will be to achive a better balance between capacities and demand in south-east France," Shell said in a press release.
Jeremy Hudson, oil analyst at Salomon Brothers in London, said: "I take it from that (the statement) that Berre is part of the closure package, although that is something of a speculative view."
The Shell statement also said the company would ensure supplies of feedstocks to its petrochemical plant, also located in Berre l'Etang.
Hudson added: "If closure is planned in Berre, that is why they had to confirm the supply of chemicals feedstocks."
